142.solution: The angular width \(\dfrac{2\lambda}{a}\) depends on the wavelength and slit width only, not on the distance to the screen (which affects the linear width).

143.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
143.solution: Resolving power \(\dfrac{2\mu\sin\theta}{\lambda}\) rises with the refractive index of the medium (as in oil immersion).

144.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
144.solution: The first secondary maximum is at \(a\sin\theta = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2}\). So \(a_1 = 3\lambda\) and \(a_2 = \dfrac{3\lambda}{\sqrt{2}}\), a change of \(3\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\lambda\).

145.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
145.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
145.solution: \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}\): the \(\alpha\)-particle has \(mq\) 8 times the proton's, so \(\dfrac{\lambda_\alpha}{\lambda_p} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{8}}\).

148.solution: The half-life is 2 days, so 16 days is 8 half-lives: \(x = \dfrac{1}{2^8} = \dfrac{1}{256}\).

149.solution: \(A + B\) is the OR operation: the output is 1 when either input or both are 1.

150.subtopic: p-n Junction — Depletion Layer and Biasing
150.solution: Reverse bias pulls the carriers away from the junction, widening the depletion region; forward bias narrows it.
